sentences.text: Virendra Singh Nagar vs State Of U.P. on 16 January, 2023

Author: Dinesh Kumar Singh
Bench: Dinesh Kumar Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 87
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 12207 of 2021
Applicant :- Virendra Singh Nagar

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Shailesh Upadhyay,Vishakha Pande
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Kaushalendra Nath Singh
Hon'ble Dinesh Kumar Singh,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Kaushalendra Nath Singh, learned counsel for the
Noida Authority and perused the record.

2.  The present application under Section 438 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant seeking bail in anticipation of his arrest in Case Crime No.581 of 2021, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120B IPC and Section 13(1)(a) of Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, Police Station- Noida Sector-20, District Gautam Budh Nagar.

entities.text: Police Station- Noida Sector-20, District Gautam Budh Nagar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. One Fundan's land holding in Khasra Nos. 684, 694, 714, 703 total areas 10-15-15 Bigha was acquired on 24th November, 1982.
The compensation for this land was given to the land holder by the Land Acquisition Officer on 27.12.21983 at the rate of 10.12 per square yard.
However, the land holder was not satisfied with this award of compensation, he filed a Reference No. 41 of 1985 before the District Judge Ghaziabad.

Vide the judgement and order dated 28th May, 1993 passed in the Virendra Singh Nagar vs State Of U.P. on 16 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29991974/
1 aforesaid reference, the rate of compensation was enhanced to Rs.16.61 per square yard.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In pursuance to the reference order, the entire compensation amount for land acquisition for the said Fundan Lal son of Chhote was deposited.
4. The land holder did not file any appeal against the said reference order before the High Court.
However, in the year 2015, he filed a First Appeal Defective No. 175 of 2015 before this Court.
This Court vide the order dated 8th July, 2015 dismissed the said appeal on the ground of inordinate delay and latches.
This appeal was filed as the Noida Authority took a decision to settle the matters which were pending either before the reference court or the High Court by mutual consent.

Therefore, this appeal came to be filed so that on the ground of pendency of appeal, the said land owner should get higher compensation than which he had accepted long back in the year 1993 after decision in the reference case.
5.

On 23rd September, 2015, the said land owner moved an application to the Noida Authority stating that his appeal was pending before the High Court and other land holders had been given compensation at the rate of Rs.297 per square yard and therefore, he should also be given the same compensation.

On this application, the present accused applicant, who was posted as Assistant Law Officer gave his report stating that since the appeal filed by the land owner was pending, the land owner be given higher compensation.
In pursuance to the said report, the land owner was given compensation of Rs.297 per square yard and he received Rs.7,26,80,427/- as further compensation.

6. Looking at the said fact that the accused applicant recommended for higher compensation of Rs.7,26,80,427/- to the accused applicant on the incorrect and false ground that the appeal was pending in the High Court, this Court finds that the offences committed by the accused-applicant does not call for an order of granting him anticipatory bail.

The accused applicant has allegedly caused wrongful loss to the Noida Authority and wrongful gain to himself and the said land owner.
7.
In view thereof, the present application has no merit and it is hereby dismissed.

Order Date :- 16.1.2023 A.Kr.
